2027-06-19.title: Saturday of the fourth week after Pentecost · Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha (St Jude the Apostle)
readings: “See, God, I have come to do your will”: sanctified through the offering of the body of Christ
Do not resist an evildoer; go the second mile; love your enemies
2027-06-19.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. The Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) is being kept; it ends with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June. The Panchangam remembers today Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, St Jude Thaddaeus, one of the Twelve.
2027-06-19.verse: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
theo: The Letter to the Hebrews lets us overhear what the Son said as he came into the world. Taking the words of a psalm, he says to the Father: “Sacrifices and offerings you have not desired, but a body you have prepared for me; in burnt offerings and sin offerings you have taken no pleasure. Then I said, ‘See, God, I have come to do your will, O God.’” This is the prayer of the Incarnation. The body that the Father prepared was formed in the womb of the Virgin Mary, and from the first moment it was a body offered: a life lived entirely to do the Father's will, from the manger to the Cross. “And it is by God's will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.” The animal sacrifices could not reach the heart; what pleases God is a will joined to his. St Augustine wrote that Christ is at once the priest who offers and the offering itself, and that he wished the Church's daily sacrifice to be the sign of this, so that the Church, being his body, learns to offer herself through him (City of God 10, in substance). That is why the Holy Qurbono is not a show we watch but a sacrifice we enter: we bring our bodies, our work and our fasting, and place them with his. On this Saturday of the Apostles' Fast, let your prayer be the same as his: “See, I have come to do your will.”

The Gospel shows what doing the Father's will looks like when someone strikes us. “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’” That old law was not cruel; it was a limit, given to stop revenge from growing larger than the injury. Jesus goes further: “But I say to you, Do not resist an evildoer. But if anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other also; and if anyone wants to sue you and take your coat, give your cloak as well; and if anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile.” In his time a soldier could force a civilian to carry his pack for a mile. Jesus says: carry it two. He is not asking us to approve of injustice; when he himself was struck before the high priest, he asked, “why do you strike me?” He is asking us to break the chain of evil by refusing to pay it back in the same coin. And then the summit: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.” This is exactly what the body prepared for him did on the Cross, where he prayed for those who crucified him. A fast from food is good; a fast from revenge, from the sharp reply, from the grudge we feed every night, is better still.

Today the Panchangam remembers Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, St Jude, one of the Twelve. Matthew and Mark call him Thaddaeus; Luke calls him Judas son of James. The Gospel of John remembers one question he asked at the Last Supper: “Lord, how is it that you will reveal yourself to us, and not to the world?” Jesus answered: “Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.” Jude wanted a great revelation; Jesus promised a home. Christian tradition remembers him as a preacher of the Gospel in the East and a martyr, and links him with the short Letter of Jude, which urges the faithful to “contend for the faith that was once for all entrusted to the saints” and to “keep yourselves in the love of God.” Because his name was so like that of the traitor, he was for centuries less invoked; yet the faithful came to love him as the helper in desperate causes, and in many parishes of Kerala people come to novenas in his honour with burdens that seem hopeless. He teaches us that no question is too bold to bring to Jesus, and no situation too dark for the God who comes to make his home with those who love him.
outline: Ask: when someone hurts me, do I pay back in the same coin, or do I go the second mile?
Point 1 · A body you have prepared for me
The prayer of the Incarnation: Christ comes to do the Father's will and offers himself once for all.
Jesus breaks the chain of revenge: turn the cheek, give the cloak, love the enemy.
The apostle who asked a question and received the promise of God's indwelling.
“Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
live: Pray for one who hurt you (Matthew 5:44)
Name before God one person who has wronged you, and pray for his or her good today, sincerely, even if your feelings do not follow yet.
Write down the intention that seems most hopeless to you and place it before the Lord, asking the prayers of St Jude.
2027-06-19.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, when you came into the world you said to the Father: see, I have come to do your will; and by the offering of your body once for all you have made us holy. Teach us to join our will to yours, to refuse the way of revenge, to go the second mile and to love even our enemies. Through the prayers of your apostle Mar Yuda Thaddai, who asked how you would reveal yourself, come with the Father and make your home in us. Help all who feel that their cause is hopeless, and keep us in your love. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The body prepared for the Son and offered once for all is given on our altar: in the Holy Qurbono we receive him who did the Father's will to the end, and we learn to offer ourselves with him, even for those who wrong us.
conn: Hebrews 10:1–4, read yesterday, said that animal sacrifices could not take away sins; today's passage gives the answer: the obedience of the Son made flesh.
Psalm 40:6–8: Hebrews puts these words in the mouth of Christ, Here I am; I delight to do your will, O my God.
John 14:22–23: Judas (not Iscariot) asks how Jesus will reveal himself; Jesus promises that the Father and the Son will make their home with those who love him.

quick: Hebrews: coming into the world, Christ said, “See, God, I have come to do your will”; we are sanctified by the offering of his body once for all.
Jesus: do not resist an evildoer; turn the other cheek, go the second mile, love your enemies.
Today we remember Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, St Jude, one of the Twelve, invoked as a helper in desperate causes.
2027-06-19.action: Do one kind thing today for someone who has been unkind to you.
2027-06-19.question: Whom do I still need to forgive, and will I pray for that person today?

family.explain: Jesus teaches us something very hard: not to hit back when someone hurts us, but to be kind instead, and even to pray for people who are unkind to us. This is what Jesus did on the Cross. Today we also remember St Jude, one of Jesus' twelve apostles. Many people pray to him when they have big problems, because he reminds us that nothing is impossible for God.
family.intention: We pray for people who are angry with each other, in families, in our neighbourhood and in the world, that they may make peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone who hurt us whom we can forgive and pray for tonight?”

illus: A bus conductor on the Kottayam route was insulted every day for a month by the same passenger, a young man who refused to pay the full fare and mocked him in front of everyone. The conductor's friends told him to throw the boy off the bus. One morning the young man boarded pale and shaking; his mother had been taken to the medical college hospital in the night. The conductor saw that he had no money at all. Without a word he punched a ticket, put it in his hand, and at the hospital stop he walked him to the gate. A week later the young man came back to the bus, paid his fare, and said quietly: you went the second mile for me. The conductor only smiled. He told his family that evening that he had been praying for the boy every night of the Apostles' Fast.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came to do the Father's will and loved your enemies to the end. Give us hearts that do not pay back evil with evil, and with St Jude, teach us to trust you in every need. Amen.
share: See, God, I have come to do your will (Hebrews 10:7). Where is the Father's will hardest for me to accept just now?
If anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). Where can I go the second mile this week?
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). Whom do I find it hardest to pray for?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to love as you love.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a sign of reconciliation in a world divided by revenge.
For all who are persecuted for their faith, and for those who persecute them.
For families and neighbours divided by quarrels, that someone may take the first step to peace.
For all who bring desperate needs to the prayers of St Jude, that they may find help and hope.
For all who keep the Apostles' Fast, that they may fast also from anger and revenge.
pm.close: Father, your Son came into the world to do your will and offered his body for us once for all. Make us one with his obedience and his love, that we may overcome evil with good. Through the prayers of the apostle Mar Yuda Thaddai, help us in every need and make your home in us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

kidsaint: St Jude, the apostle with a question

St Jude was one of Jesus' twelve apostles. At the Last Supper he asked Jesus a question: Lord, why will you show yourself to us and not to the whole world? Jesus gave him a beautiful answer: if you love me and keep my word, my Father and I will come and live in your heart. Today many people pray to St Jude when they have very big problems, because he reminds us that God is always near. Lesson: you can ask Jesus any question and bring him any problem.

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews tells us what Jesus said when he came into the world: a body you have prepared for me; then I said, ‘See, God, I have come to do your will, O God’ (Hebrews 10:5, 7). Jesus took a body from the Virgin Mary to offer it for us. And it is by God's will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all (Hebrews 10:10).

In the Gospel Jesus shows what doing the Father's will means. You have heard, an eye for an eye; but I say to you, do not resist an evildoer; turn the other cheek; go also the second mile (Matthew 5:38–41). Jesus is not saying that evil does not matter. He is teaching us to stop the chain of revenge. And he goes even further: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). That is what he did on the Cross.

Today we remember Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, St Jude, one of the Twelve. At the Last Supper he asked: Lord, how is it that you will reveal yourself to us, and not to the world? Jesus answered: those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:22–23). Many people today come to St Jude with problems that seem hopeless. He points them to the God who makes his home in us.

In this Apostles' Fast, let us fast also from revenge. Let us pray for someone who has hurt us, go the second mile for someone who does not deserve it, and bring our hardest intentions to the Lord with St Jude. Amen.
kids: Children, what do you do when someone pushes you or says something bad to you? It is easy to push back. But Jesus says: do not hit back; be kind instead, and pray for that person. That is very hard! But Jesus did it on the Cross, when he prayed for the people who hurt him. Today we also remember St Jude, a friend of Jesus. Many people ask St Jude to pray for them when they have big problems. Tonight, say a prayer for someone who was not kind to you. Jesus will be very happy.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
On the memory of Mar Yuda Thaddai Shleeha, in the Apostles' Fast: the body offered to do the Father's will, the second mile, and the apostle who asked a question.

points.h: See, I have come to do your will
sub: A body prepared by the Father.
From the manger to the Cross.
Our wills joined to his in the Qurbono.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work.
points.apply: Begin each day of the fast with the words: See, Lord, I have come to do your will.

sub: An eye for an eye was a limit.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Do one concrete good this week for someone who has wronged you.

points.h: Mar Yuda Thaddai: the apostle who asked
q: Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.
But you, beloved, build yourselves up on your most holy faith; pray in the Holy Spirit; keep yourselves in the love of God
points.apply: Bring your hardest intention to the Lord today, with the prayers of St Jude, and leave it with him.

concl: The Son came to do the Father's will, and doing it led him to love his enemies to the end.
St Jude asked how Jesus would show himself; the answer is love that keeps his word.
2027-06-19.resolve: In this fast, fast from revenge: go the second mile and pray for those who hurt you.
